newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu vows to curb state in Israeli economy.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu vows to curb state in Israeli economy.

text.p: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said on Saturday his government was about to embark on a sweeping programme of liberalisation and privatisation.
"By the end of four years, we'll be a different country," Netanyahu told the opening of the international Jerusalem Business Conference.

Netanyahu did not detail plans but hinted deregulation may include public transportation, energy and the sale of state-owned broadcasting media. "If you are prepared to buy media, we are going to privatise them," he said.
Netanyahu denied a slowdown in the peace process since he took office in June was discouraging foreign investors, who injected some $2 billion into Israel's economy in 1995.
"The smartest money is coming to Israel...and they say we want to buy," he said. "Those who are sitting on the fence waiting for peace will come down, because peace will come."
Netanyahu said if a full programme of liberalisation and privatisation were implemented, Israel's per capita gross domestic product would double over the next 10 years from the current $16,000.
